Our Administration also expanded access to naloxone and other life-saving interventions, including working with Congress to remove barriers that prevented medical professionals from prescribing treatment for opioid use disorder.

President Biden ran for office to restore the soul of our nation – and he has been clear that hate, bigotry, and violence have no place here in the U.S. 
 
That’s why our Administration has taken numerous steps to counter hate in all its forms. In 2021, President Biden signed into law the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act, which includes the Khalid Jabara and Heather Heyer NO HATE Act, to improve the reporting and prevention of hate crimes and ensure that hate crimes information is more accessible to Asian American and Pacific Islander Communities. Attorney General Merrick Garland also appointed the Justice Department’s first-ever Anti-Hate Crimes Resources Coordinator and designated staff to oversee expedited review of hate crimes. And, the Federal Bureau of Investigation has elevated hate crimes and criminal civil rights violations to its highest-level national threat priority.
 
In 2022, President Biden hosted the first-ever White House United We Stand Summit to address hate-fueled violence and put forward a shared vision for working toward a more united America. At the Summit, President Biden announced the White House Initiative to Counter Hate-Motivated Violence to address violence and bias against all communities.
 
President Biden also established an interagency group to increase and better coordinate federal efforts to counter Antisemitism, Islamophobia, and related forms of bias and discrimination within the U.S. In 2023, amidst a historic increase in antisemitic incidents, President Biden released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Antisemitism. In 2024, he released the first-ever U.S. National Strategy to Counter Islamophobia and Anti-Arab Hate.
 
The power is within each of us to rise together against hate and build a nation that treats everyone with dignity and respect.

Earlier this evening, FEMA Administrator Deanne Criswell and Homeland Security Advisor Liz Sherwood-Randall briefed President Biden on the ongoing impacts of Hurricane Helene in multiple states, including Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Alabama, Tennessee, and Virginia. The FEMA Administrator updated the President on Federal actions to support emergency response and recovery and briefed the President on her visit today to Georgia where she surveyed damage and assessed emerging needs on the ground. Administrator Criswell will travel to North Carolina tomorrow.

The President directed Administrator Criswell to determine what more can be done to accelerate support to those who are having the most difficult time accessing assistance in isolated communities. The President also advised the FEMA Administrator that as soon as it will not disrupt emergency response operations, he intends to travel this week to impacted communities.

President Biden’s New Executive Order to Reduce Gun Violence and Save Lives

Combats Emerging Firearm Threats
- The new Emerging Firearms Threats Task Force will combat the emerging threats of machinegun conversion devices and unserialized, 3D-printed firearms. Within 90 days, the Task Force will send President Biden a risk assessment and a strategy to address these threats.

tweets.text:
Today, President Biden spoke with four individuals from across the country about how our Administration’s Investing in America agenda is benefitting their lives and planting the seeds for a brighter future for their community.
 
Here are their stories:

Mayor Woodfin from Birmingham, Alabama highlighted several projects from President Biden and Vice President Harris’s Investing in America agenda that are growing the economy and creating opportunities for Birmingham families and communities.

Jackie is a retired schoolteacher living in Muskego, Wisconsin, with her husband Doug. She has an incurable but treatable blood cancer and takes the blood thinner Xarelto, which was one of the first ten drugs Medicare negotiated a lower price for in the first year of the program. With her current Medicare insurance, Jackie’s prescription drugs can cost her tens of thousands of dollars in out-of-pocket costs per year. Because of the Biden-Harris Administration’s Inflation Reduction Act, Jackie’s out of pocket prescription drug costs will be capped at $2,000 starting next year. Jackie spoke with President Biden about how his actions to lower prescription drug costs will give her and her family breathing room in their daily lives.

Chairwoman Flores of the Colorado River Indian Tribes highlighted infrastructure investments from President Biden and Vice President Harris’s Investing in America agenda that are delivering clean water and creating more opportunity for families and the Colorado River Indian Tribes community.

Cecilia is a Philadelphia Chinatown resident. She was a widow and single mother when she learned that her community church and the school, Holy Redeemer, would be demolished for a federal highway project. Later her home would be taken via eminent domain for the Center City Commuter Rail Tunnel. She and hundreds of residents were eventually displaced, but Cecilia went on to help form the Philadelphia Chinatown Development Corporation, a nonprofit that helped develop housing for low-income Philadelphians, seniors, and help small business owners. She never gave up on her dream of capping the dangerous Vine Street Expressway. Thanks to President Biden’s Inflation Reduction Act and the Reconnecting Communities program, her dream will come true.

Our Administration will continue to deliver direct results in communities across the country.

The United States has been closely monitoring Venezuela’s presidential election that took place on Sunday, July 28 and the subsequent announcements by Venezuela’s National Electoral Council.

We continue to call for Venezuela’s electoral authorities to release full, transparent, and detailed voting results, including by polling station.  This is especially critical given that there are clear signs that the election results announced by Venezuela’s National Electoral Council do not reflect the will of the Venezuelan people as it was expressed at the ballot box on July 28.  We are also reviewing other electoral data shared by civil society organizations and the reports of international election monitors. 

The United States stands on the side of the democratic aspirations of the Venezuela people, including supporting their right to express their views freely and without reprisal.

I am grateful to our Allies who stood with us throughout tough, complex negotiations to achieve this outcome— including Germany, Poland, Slovenia, Norway, and Turkey. This week, the Supreme Court upheld the federal law that prohibits domestic abusers under a restraining order from purchasing or possessing a gun.

Before President Biden’s Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, the federal law prohibiting convicted domestic abusers from having guns did not apply to dating partners. And nearly 30 years of homicide data shows that in fatal domestic violence incidents, nearly half of the women killed by intimate partners were in a dating relationship.

President Biden’s Bipartisan Safer Communities Act finally narrowed the “boyfriend loophole” – now, people convicted of abusing a dating partner are also prohibited from purchasing or possessing firearms.

This is a real, life-saving step.

G7 Leaders’ Statement on Gaza

We, the Leaders of the Group of Seven (G7), fully endorse and will stand behind the comprehensive deal outlined by President Biden that would lead to an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, the release of all hostages, a significant and sustained increase in humanitarian assistance for distribution throughout Gaza, and an enduring end to the crisis, with Israel’s security interests and Gazan civilian safety assured. We reaffirm our support for a credible pathway towards peace leading to a two State solution.

We call on Hamas to accept this deal, that Israel is ready to move forward with, and we urge countries with influence over Hamas to help ensure that it does so.

media.alt_text: Richard: I am texting you to give you a personal note of thanks for signing the PACT Act in August of 2022. I served in the military from September 1986 through December 2009. Served in Iraq in 2004. Was exposed to the burn pits. Was diagnosed with Stage Four colon cancer in October 2023. Been doing very well with chemo since then. Because of the PACT Act, I was able to receive 100% disability through the VA and receive the care and treatment and financial assistance I needed to get better. The PACT Act practically saved my life and I am truly grateful to you and Congress for signing the PACT Act for all of our service members and their families. Again, thank you from the bottom of my heart.

Ken: Dear Mr. President, Thank you for visiting New Hampshire, you were right around the corner. The PACT Act is one of the best things that has helped veterans in a long time. Keep up the support for veterans! Thank you!!!

tweets.text:
The Biden-Harris Administration welcomes the steps to increase humanitarian aid deliveries announced by the Israeli government tonight at @POTUS’ request following his call with Prime Minister Netanyahu.

These steps, including a commitment to open the Ashdod port for the direct delivery of assistance into Gaza, to open the Erez crossing for a new route for assistance to reach north Gaza, and to significantly increase deliveries from Jordan directly into Gaza, must now be fully and rapidly implemented.

As the President said today, U.S. policy with respect to Gaza will be determined by our assessment of Israel’s immediate action on these and other steps, including steps to protect innocent civilians and the safety of aid workers.

The United States Government is prepared to work in full coordination with the Government of Israel, the Governments of Jordan and Egypt, the United Nations, and humanitarian organizations, to ensure that these important steps are implemented and result in a significant increase in humanitarian assistance reaching civilians in dire need throughout Gaza over the coming days and weeks.

On the 14th anniversary of the signing of the Affordable Care Act, the results are clear.
 
Under President Biden, more Americans have health insurance than under any President.

21 million Americans signed up for health coverage this year
- That includes 1.7 million Black Americans and 3.4 million Latino Americans
- A majority of shoppers found coverage for less than $10 a month

President Biden is not resting on his accomplishments, he has a bold agenda to continue to bring down Americans’ health care costs.
- Calling on Congress to make expanded Affordable Care Act tax credits permanent
- Lowering prescription drug prices
- Fighting to increase the number of drugs Medicare can negotiate on for lower prices
- Working to expand $35 a month insulin and a $2,000 out of pocket cap on drug spending to everyone

And despite Republican elected officials fighting to get rid of the Affordable Care Act – President Biden has been clear:
 
He will always protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, Medicare, and Medicaid.

President Biden’s full statement: https://t.co/f3tsIm5LM0

media.alt_text:
Two years ago tomorrow, shortly before dawn, Russian missiles began exploding near the capital city of Kyiv. Russian troops marched across the border into Ukraine. Vladimir Putin’s vicious onslaught against Ukraine had begun. 

He believed that he could easily bend the will and break the resolve of a free people. That he could roll into a sovereign nation, and the world would roll over. That he could shake the foundations of security in Europe and beyond. 

Two years later, we see even more vividly what we’ve known since day one: Putin miscalculated badly.

The brave people of Ukraine fight on, unbowed in their determination to defend their freedom and future. NATO is stronger, larger, and more united than ever. And the unprecedented 50-nation global coalition in support of Ukraine, led by the United States, remains committed to providing critical assistance to Ukraine and holding Russia accountable for its aggression.

The American people and people around the world understand that the stakes of this fight extend far beyond Ukraine. Ten years ago, Putin occupied Crimea, and created puppet regimes in Ukraine’s Luhansk and Donetsk regions.  Two years ago, he tried to wipe Ukraine off the map.  If Putin does not pay the price for his death and destruction, he will keep going. And the costs to the United States—along with our NATO Allies and partners in Europe and around the world—will rise.

Today, I am announcing more than 500 new sanctions against Russia for its ongoing war of conquest on Ukraine and for the death of Aleksey Navalny, who was a courageous anti-corruption activist and Putin’s fiercest opposition leader. These sanctions will target individuals connected to Navalny’s imprisonment as well as Russia’s financial sector, defense industrial base, procurement networks and sanctions evaders across multiple continents.

Two years into this war, the people of Ukraine continue to fight with tremendous courage. But they are running out of ammunition. Ukraine needs more supplies from the United States to hold the line against Russia’s relentless attacks, which are enabled by arms and ammunition from Iran and North Korea. That’s why the House of Representatives must pass the bipartisan national security supplemental bill, before it’s too late.

This bill provides urgent funding for Ukraine. It also invests in America’s own defense industrial base. It passed overwhelmingly in the Senate, and there is no question that, if the Speaker called a vote, it would pass quickly in the House. Congress knows that by supporting this bill, we can strengthen security in Europe, strengthen our security at home, and stand up to Putin. Opposing this bill only plays into his hands.

media.alt_text:
Aranka  
10/17/23
To: POTUS
Dear Mr. President and Mrs. Vice President, 
I just opened a notice.... I let it sit about a week and a half before opening, because I knew it would tell me how much I would have to start repaying each month, which would be an amount I could not afford to pay at this time. Instead, what it said was... that my student loans have been forgiven in full. Around $38k. I am overwhelmed. I am overwhelmed with gratitude. I have always had faith in our system, but lately, well. It's been difficult. It's easy to lose faith in our current system. But today, I can say that the system has tangibly changed my life for the better... And I very sincerely thank you for it. You don't know what this means to me.
Thank you,
Aranka

media.alt_text:
President Joseph R. Biden, Jr. spoke today with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel to discuss developments in Gaza and in the surrounding region.
 
The President welcomed the first two convoys of humanitarian assistance since Hamas’s October 7 terrorist attack, which crossed the border into Gaza and is being distributed to Palestinians in need.  The leaders affirmed that there will now be continued flow of this critical assistance into Gaza. Lowering Prescription Drug Costs Under the Biden-Harris Administration

- 9 million: Number of seniors who took the 10 drugs selected for Medicare Price Negotiation in 2022.  
- $3.4 billion: Amount Medicare beneficiaries spent in out of pocket costs in 2022 on the 10 drugs.
- $6,497: The out-of-pocket cost seniors had to pay per year for just one of the drugs selected for negotiation

- 4 million: Number of seniors already benefitting from the Inflation Reduction Act’s $35 per month cap on the cost of insulin.
